title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: Build an academic career in technology, AI and data-protection law through sustained scholarship, teaching, interdisciplinary research, doctoral supervision and policy engagement.

facts.Timeline assumption: The student already holds a Ph.D., so the next normal steps are faculty, postdoctoral, research and visiting-scholar appointments rather than another master's. Academic appointment and promotion requirements vary by institution and jurisdiction.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Establish a strong technology-law publication and teaching record and compete for faculty, postdoctoral and research appointments.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop a recognised niche such as AI governance, data protection, platform regulation, cybersecurity law, digital competition or algorithmic accountability.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead interdisciplinary research, supervise doctoral candidates, secure research funding and advise institutions on technology regulation.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become an established technology-law scholar who can evaluate emerging AI and data technologies alongside legal, economic, social and governance consequences.

rows.text: Prepare 3 complete lecture modules covering technology law, AI governance and data protection

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Technology-law scholarship needs continuous updating. Maintain legal depth while learning enough about AI systems, data architecture, cybersecurity and algorithmic evaluation to challenge technical assumptions and assess real-world regulatory consequences.
Because the student already has a Ph.D., postdoctoral research, visiting fellowships and faculty/research collaborations are generally more relevant than student internships.

blocks.label: Visa and job-offer note
blocks.text: Academic employment is distinct from legal practice. A law professor may not need local professional admission for teaching/research, but the exact employment and visa rules must be checked with the destination institution and immigration authority.
Career progression
Typical progression can be approximately 0–3 years → 3–7 years → 7–12 years → 12–18+ years, but actual promotion depends on institutional rules, publications, teaching, research funding and service.
Ph.D./advanced research routes
Since the student already has a Ph.D.:

The long-term objective is to become an established scholar in a clearly defined technology-law field. A senior professor should combine legal scholarship with enough technical understanding to evaluate AI systems, data practices and digital infrastructure, while maintaining strong teaching, doctoral supervision, research funding, international collaboration and policy engagement.
